premises: Deformation twinning and dislocation slip can be spatially and synergistically coordinated in CoCrFeNi nanopillars.
This coordination promotes deformation delocalization and delays necking failure.
The coordination originates from atomic-level chemical heterogeneities causing wide variations in stacking fault energy.
The result is ultrahigh uniform tensile ductility (~110%) at high flow stress (0.6–1.0 GPa) in <110>-oriented single-crystalline nanopillars.
